claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is single-phase fcc.
A 10 nm L1₀ FePt layer will be deposited on the FeCoNiCrMn alloy.
The FePt layer will be sputtered at room temperature.
The coated alloy will be annealed at 700°C for 1 hour in vacuum.
The deposited and annealed 10 nm FePt layer will have the ordered L1₀ structure.
The L1₀ FePt layer will act as a hard magnetic layer with high magnetic anisotropy.
Introducing the hard FePt layer will increase the magnetic anisotropy of the high-entropy alloy.
The increase in magnetic anisotropy will increase coercivity.
The intervention will produce a coercive field of at least 600 Oe.
The coercive field will increase relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative.
The FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy alloy must remain single-phase fcc after processing.
The FePt layer must be compatible with the high-entropy alloy.
A coated and an uncoated FeCoNiCrMn alloy can be compared by VSM or SQUID measurements of their magnetic hysteresis loops and coercive fields.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a coercive field of at least 600 Oe, but the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant increase over the control. A result significantly above the control but below 600 Oe would miss the predicted threshold without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
